docs.title: Cobblemon Picnic
docs.text:
Spawn-hunting, made cozy. Place a Picnic Table, left-click it, and the wild Pokémon around you are despawned and re-rolled into a fresh maximised spawn — hunt a shiny or a specific species without walking the map raw. It doubles as a social station: shiny aura, Pokémon care and trainer battles.

MC 1.21.1 Fabric NeoForge Cobblemon 1.8+

Get started Picnic tables

docs.title: What can it do?
docs.text:
• Spawn re-rolling — clear the wild Pokémon around you and roll a fresh batch, on demand.
  • Three table tiers — Basic, Advanced and Expert, each bigger and cheaper to re-roll than the last.
  • Special baskets — put one in an Expert table to picnic underwater, in the Nether or the End, hunt alphas, or summon trainers.
  • Shiny aura — sit together and everyone's shiny odds go up. A full table doubles them.
  • Items & care — wash and play with your Pokémon, and store bread in baskets.
  • Troubleshooting — a re-roll that spawned nothing, fliers that vanish, and what the game's messages mean.
  • Commands & config — tune every number in game, and read the statistics of every re-roll you've ever made.

docs.title: Get it
docs.text:
Download Modrinth · CurseForge · What changed Version 5.1.3 Minecraft 1.21.1 Side Server and every player's game Cobblemon 1.8+ Fabric Architectury API, Fabric Language Kotlin NeoForge Architectury API, Kotlin for Forge Optional Cloth Config: the settings screen (with Mod Menu on Fabric) · Roughly Enough Items: each item's colours fold into one expandable recipe entry

New here? Start with Getting Started.

docs.title: Commands & Config
docs.text:
Everything lives under one command: /picnic.

/picnic                                           # print every setting (anyone)
/picnic config                                    # the same listing, for an operator
/picnic config <feature>                          # one feature's settings (operator)
/picnic config <feature> <setting> <value>        # change one (operator)
/picnic config <feature> <setting> default        # put it back to its default (operator)
/picnic config <feature> reset                    # put the whole feature back (operator)
/picnic stats                                     # picnic statistics (anyone)
/picnic stats player|dimension|species <value>    # one slice of them (anyone)
/picnic stats shiny                               # just the shinies (anyone)
/picnic stats reset                               # clear the aggregates (operator)
/picnic reload                                    # re-read the config file from disk (operator)
/picnic reset                                     # restore every default (operator)

default works on every setting — you never have to look up what the shipped value was.

docs.title: /picnic config — the settings
docs.text:
Reading them is open to everyone through /picnic: knowing the shiny-aura multiplier and the re-roll cooldown you're playing under is part of playing. Changing anything needs operator rank.

Every feature has an enabled switch, so a server can keep the picnic and drop any part of it.

/picnic config shinyaura multiplier 3             # a full table triples shiny odds
/picnic config shinyaura multiplier default       # back to ×2
/picnic config reroll enabled false               # switch the spawn re-roll off entirely
/picnic config reroll spawncap expert 16          # per-tier settings take the tier in the middle
/picnic config reroll protectshiny expert true    # per-rung settings take the rung
/picnic config wash reset                         # every washing setting back to its default

Tiers and rungs are both basic, advanced and expert. A Diving, Hot or Strange table still standing from before 5.0.0 uses the expert values.

docs.title: Features and their settings
docs.text:
Feature Setting Value What it does reroll enabled true/false The spawn re-roll itself. Default on. cooldown 0–3600 Seconds between re-rolls, per table and per player. Default 5. 0 disables. spawncap <tier> int Max Pokémon per re-roll for that tier. fuelcost <tier> int Bread per re-roll for that tier (7 Basic, 5 Advanced, 3 above). 0 makes it free. radius <tier> blocks How far that tier's re-roll reaches, both the area it clears and the area it fills. Default 32 Basic, 48 Advanced, 64 above. clearance 0–16 Blocks around you where nothing spawns, so a group never lands on top of you. Default 2. Picnic blocks are always off-limits. flyinglift 0–64 How high re-rolled fliers are lifted off the ground (default 12, 0 grounds them). Never changes which Pokémon spawn. flierleash 0–600 Seconds a re-rolled flier is kept within the table's re-roll radius (default 30, 0 lets it roam at once). log true/false Writes every re-roll to latest.log: what it cleared and spawned, one line per Pokémon. Default on. protectshiny <rung> true/false The re-roll keeps shiny wild Pokémon instead of despawning them. Default off. protectlegendary <rung> true/false Keeps legendary wild Pokémon. Default off. protectmythical <rung> true/false Keeps mythical wild Pokémon. Default off. protectultrabeast <rung> true/false Keeps Ultra Beast wild Pokémon. Default off. protectalpha <rung> true/false Keeps alpha wild Pokémon. Default off. platforms enabled true/false A re-roll may spawn on any floor you built (planks, quartz, concrete…), not only natural ground. Default off. snackbias enabled true/false A re-roll borrows the spawn influences of a nearby seasoned poke-snack. Default off. tmteach enabled true/false Party move teaching on a re-roll. Default on. chance 0..1 Chance per re-roll. Default 0.05. tm true/false TM moves may be taught. Default on. tutor true/false Tutor moves may be taught. Default on. egg true/false Egg moves may be taught. Default on. alphaboost enabled true/false The Alpha Basket. Off: a table with one re-rolls normally. Default on. chance 0..1 Chance each Pokémon of an Alpha Basket re-roll is an alpha. Default 0.10. batch 1–100 Percent of the batch an Alpha Basket re-roll still spawns. Default 50. shinyaura enabled true/false The Shiny Aura. Default on. multiplier 1–100 How many times better your shiny odds get at a full table. Default 2 (double). deploy enabled true/false Sitting down sends out your party. Default on. mindistance 0–32 Closest a party member lands, in blocks. Default 4. maxdistance 0–32 Furthest a party member lands. Default 7. Each Pokémon rolls its own distance in the band, and a max below the min is raised to it. peaceful enabled true/false While someone is seated, hostile mobs flee the table. Default on. radius 0–128 How far that reaches, in blocks. Default 30. wash enabled true/false Washing, from the wheel or with a Poke-sponge. Default on. friendship int Friendship gained from a wash. cooldown seconds Wait between washes, per Pokémon. Default 3. requirestable true/false Need a nearby table to wash. Off also shows the option on the wheel everywhere. blockinbattle true/false Washing is refused during a battle (a Cobblemon battle or an Action Combat fight). Default on. play enabled true/false Playing fetch, from the wheel or with a thrown Fetchball. Default on. friendship int Friendship gained from a game. breakchance 0..1 Chance a slime ball splatters. A Fetchball ignores this. cooldown seconds Wait between games, per Pokémon. Default 3. requirestable true/false Need a nearby table to play. Off also shows the option on the wheel everywhere. blockinbattle true/false Playing and the Fetchball are refused during a battle. Default on. battleseeker enabled true/false The Combat Basket (it kept the name of the Battle Seeker it replaced). Off: a table with one summons no trainer. Default on. blockinbattle true/false The Combat Basket re-roll is refused while you are already in a battle. Default on. matchlevel true/false Scale summoned trainers to your party's level. Default on. levelgap int Level offset for summoned trainers. Default 8. hazards enabled true/false What a table and its basket carry between dimensions — burning, scorching, flooding and drifting. Off, every table is plain furniture. Default on. reigrouping enabled true/false With REI installed, folds each table wood, the coloured baskets and the benches into one expandable REI entry. Client-side: it groups your own game's REI list, applied on REI's next reload (F3+T). Default on. table light 0–15 Light level emitted by the table. Re-place a table to relight it. actiondistance 0–512 How close a table has to be for the table-gated actions. Default 25.

The five protect… settings are opt-in and granular: turn on only the rarities you want the re-roll to spare, on only the rungs you want. peaceful is on by default: sit at a table and hostile mobs within radius blocks lose their target and run away, like a creeper fleeing a cat.

docs.title: /picnic stats
docs.text:
Available to everyone. Shows a summary of picnic activity:

  • Total re-rolls, Pokémon spawned / despawned
  • Shinies found (with ratio), legendaries / mythicals, alphas
  • Snacks consumed, distinct species
  • Most common and rarest species
/picnic stats          # show the summary
/picnic stats reset    # (operator) clear the aggregates

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Ask for one slice instead of the lot. Each filter reports its own re-roll count, what came out, and the shiny rate for that slice alone — and for shinies, the species, level and coordinates of each one. All of them are open to everyone.

/picnic stats player <name>       # everything one trainer's re-rolls produced
/picnic stats dimension <id>      # e.g. minecraft:the_nether
/picnic stats species <name>      # every appearance of one species
/picnic stats shiny               # just the shinies, and where they turned up

species tab-completes from what the log has actually seen. player and dimension are free text, so you can ask about someone who's offline or a dimension that isn't loaded right now.

Statistics persist in config/cobblemon_picnic_stats.json (aggregates) and config/cobblemon_picnic_events.jsonl (a granular per-re-roll log). The summary reads the aggregates; the filters replay the log, which is the only place the per-re-roll detail survives — so a filter can look back further than the last stats reset.

docs.title: The settings screen
docs.text:
With Cloth Config installed, the same values are editable in a GUI — on Fabric via Mod Menu → Cobblemon Picnic → Settings, on NeoForge via the Config button in the mods list. Its pages:

Page What's on it General Re-roll switch and cooldown, light level, party deploy and its distances, flier lift and leash, spawn clearance, re-roll log, action distance Tiers Spawn cap, fuel cost and re-roll radius for Basic, Advanced and Expert Shiny Aura The aura switch and the full-table multiplier, with the ladder it works out to Interactions Washing, playing fetch (each with its "blocked in battle" switch), and party move teaching (chance, and TM / tutor / egg moves) Baskets The Combat Basket (switch, blocked in battle, level match, level gap), the Alpha Basket (switch, chance, batch), the dimension hazards and REI colour grouping Protection & seating What a re-roll keeps (shiny, legendary, mythical, Ultra Beast, alpha) per rung, snack bias, built platforms, and mobs fleeing a seated table

⚠️ On a server that screen only edits your own game's file, and says so at the top. Use /picnic config to change the settings everyone plays under.

docs.title: The config file
docs.text:
config/cobblemon_picnic.json          # settings
config/cobblemon_picnic_stats.json    # statistics aggregates
config/cobblemon_picnic_events.jsonl  # granular per-re-roll log

Edit the first by hand if you like, then apply it with /picnic reload — no restart needed. If the file can't be read, /picnic reload says why and changes nothing, and the mod leaves the file alone until it is fixed: settings changed in the meantime last until the server stops.

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text:
Tier Spawn cap Fuel/re-roll Radius Seats Basic 5 7 32 2 Advanced 8 5 48 3 Expert 12 3 64 4

Seat counts are fixed per tier and not configurable. Elsewhere: re-roll cooldown 5 s (per-table and per-player), party TM cross-teach 5%, full-table shiny multiplier ×2, wash and play cooldowns 3 s each (per Pokémon), party deploy 4–7 blocks, Alpha Basket 10% alphas at 50% of the batch.

docs.title: Picnic without the spawn manipulation
docs.text: /picnic config reroll enabled false switches the re-roll off entirely — right-clicking a table then spawns and despawns nothing, and costs no bread. Seats, the Shiny Aura, bread baskets and the care interactions all keep working.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Cobblemon Picnic runs on Fabric and NeoForge for Minecraft 1.21.1. Drop these in mods/:

Always Cobblemon Picnic (Modrinth · CurseForge) + Cobblemon 1.8.0 or newer Fabric Architectury API + Fabric Language Kotlin (Architectury brings Fabric API with it) NeoForge Architectury API + Kotlin for Forge Optional Cloth Config for the settings screen, plus Mod Menu on Fabric. JEI or REI to browse recipes: each special basket has its own entry, and with REI each table wood, the coloured baskets and the benches fold into one expandable entry (reigrouping)

Older Cobblemon (1.7.x) is not supported: the game stops at the loader's dependency screen and names Cobblemon, instead of crashing later.

On a dedicated server, configure it with the commands — the settings screen only edits your own client's file.

docs.title: Your first table
docs.text:
• 1 · Craft it

    Three components — a Table, a Dining Bench and a Picnic Basket — then combine them with a Vivichoke, a Campfire Pot and a Campfire. The Table you use sets its cloth colour and its frame wood; each Bench becomes one of its seats.

    Full grids

  • 2 · Place it

    The table is a 3×2 multiblock that deploys in front of you, table column centred on where you aim. Face the way you want it and place. All six cells need to be free.

  • 3 · Fuel it

    Right-click a centre cell to open the GUI and put bread in the fuel slot — or leave a Picnic Basket full of bread nearby and it pulls from that.

  • 4 · Re-roll

    Left-click a centre cell. The wild Pokémon around you are cleared and a fresh batch rolls in. The GUI slider sets how many.

docs.title: One button each
docs.text:
Input On a table cell On a bench cell Right-click Opens the GUI Sit down Left-click Re-roll Break the structure

Table cells take no mining damage, so a re-roll can never destroy the table by accident. When you want the structure back in your inventory, hit a bench.

docs.title: What next?
docs.text:
• Bring friends and sit on the benches — a full table doubles everyone's shiny odds.
  • Upgrade to Expert for the biggest radius and a basket slot you can swap.
  • Going somewhere strange? There's a basket for underwater, the Nether and the End, and others for alphas and trainer battles.

docs.title: Items & Care
docs.text: Beyond re-rolling, the picnic is a place to care for your Pokémon and manage supplies.

docs.title: Pokémon care (Cobblemon interaction wheel)
docs.text:
Point at one of your Pokémon and open Cobblemon's interaction wheel — Cobblemon Picnic adds two options:

Wash 🧽Play 🟢

Wash a Pokémon → +friendship. Carry either a wet sponge, which is used up, or a Poke-sponge, which never is. Friendship gained is set by /picnic config wash friendship.

Play fetch → +friendship. Carry either a slime ball, which has a chance to splatter and be lost, or a Fetchball, which always comes back. The Pokémon sprints after the ball, tracking it as it bounces and rolls, then walks back at a normal pace with it. Tunables: friendship and breakchance, under /picnic config play.

When you carry both, the crafted item wins — you never spend a wet sponge while a Poke-sponge is in your bag.

The wheel is not the only way in. Holding the Poke-sponge, you can right-click a Pokémon to wash it there and then; and the Fetchball can simply be thrown, at nothing in particular. Both check exactly the same conditions the wheel does.

docs.title: You have to be at a picnic
docs.text:
Both options only appear on the wheel while a picnic table is in range (/picnic config table actiondistance, 25 blocks by default) — the wheel never offers something that is about to be refused. Turn requirestable off under /picnic config wash or /picnic config play and that option shows up anywhere. On a server, the wheel follows the server's settings, not your own game's.

Either one can be switched off outright with /picnic config wash enabled false or /picnic config play enabled false. The option leaves the wheel, and the Poke-sponge or the Fetchball does nothing either.

docs.title: Not during a battle
docs.text:
Washing, playing and throwing a Fetchball are refused while a battle is on: when that Pokémon is in a Cobblemon battle, or when you are in one or in a Cobblemon Action Combat fight. You are told "Your Pokémon can't do that during a battle." A Fetchball stays in your hand, no Pokémon picks one up while its owner fights, and a fetch already underway stops where it is (the ball stays on the ground). Action Combat (0.1.48 or later) is optional: without it only Cobblemon battles count.

Operators can lift the block: /picnic config wash blockinbattle false and /picnic config play blockinbattle false (Play covers the Fetchball too). Default on. Off, that action works during a battle as it did before 5.1.1.

docs.title: One Pokémon at a time
docs.text: Each option has a 3-second cooldown, counted per Pokémon (cooldown, under /picnic config wash and /picnic config play). Look after one and you can turn straight to the next; come back to the first and you wait. It's there so a single Pokémon can't be farmed for friendship, not to slow down caring for a whole team.

docs.title: Crafted care items
docs.text: Two permanent upgrades to the interactions above. Neither is ever consumed, and neither replaces anything: the plain slime ball and the wet sponge keep working exactly as they always have.

docs.title: Fetchball
docs.text:
A slime ball bound in leather and string. Play fetch with it and your Pokémon brings it back every time — it never splatters.

You can also just throw it. Right-click with the Fetchball in hand and it flies where you are looking, with no Pokémon picked beforehand and no table to stand at. Where it lands it stays, as an item on the ground that never despawns, and what happens next is up to who reaches it:

  • You walk over and pick it up → nothing. Fetching your own ball is not playing with anyone.
  • One of your Pokémon fetches it → they carry it back to your hand, and that is worth friendship. It keeps waiting while nobody comes, so sending one out after the throw still counts.

It has to be your Pokémon, within 12 blocks of you, off cooldown — and near an Advanced table if play requirestable is on. Water is no obstacle: the ball floats and they go in after it. Lava is — a Pokémon that would have to reach into it turns around and walks back to where it was standing, and the ball is gone.

➜ Ingredient Amount String 4 Leather 4 Slime Ball 1 → Fetchball 1

docs.title: Poke-sponge
docs.text:
A bath sponge that never dries out. One of them washes a whole team, forever. Right-click a Pokémon with it in hand to wash without opening the wheel.

➜ Ingredient Amount Water Bucket 2 String 2 Sponge or Wet Sponge 4 Slime Ball 1 → Poke-sponge 1

The four sponge slots take either a dry Sponge or a Wet Sponge, in any mix — no need to dry them out first. The two Water Buckets come back as empty buckets, as vanilla always returns them.

docs.title: Picnic Baskets
docs.text:
Picnic Baskets are placeable furniture available in every apricorn color. The apricorn you use picks the color, and a basket is also an ingredient of the Picnic Table itself.

➜

The apricorn and the basket cycle together: whichever colour you put in is the colour you get out.

Ingredient Amount Apricorn — any of the 7 colors 2 Apricorn Planks 2 → Picnic Basket in that color 1
  • Place one on the ground like a block.
  • Store bread inside it.
  • A nearby table pulls bread from baskets to fuel its re-rolls — so you can keep a basket stocked next to your setup instead of refilling the fuel slot.
  • Dye a placed basket with sneak + right-click, holding a dye in one of the seven basket colours. The bread inside stays where it is. A table's own basket takes a dye too — see Dyeing.
  • Craft it into a special basket — Water, Fire, Strange, Alpha or Combat — that changes what an Expert table does. See Baskets.

docs.title: poke_snack bias
docs.text:
If a seasoned poke_snack (a Cobblemon snack item with spawn influence) is on the ground near a table when you re-roll:

  • The re-roll respects the snack's spawn influence, biasing what appears.
  • One bite is consumed from the closest snack each time. That bite counts like any natural one, so the snack runs down normally and does not refill afterwards.

This lets you steer a re-roll toward the kinds of Pokémon a given snack attracts.

docs.title: Combat Basket
docs.text:
Put a Combat Basket (any Picnic Basket + iron sword) in an Expert table's basket slot and every re-roll also summons an RCT trainer to battle. The basket is never consumed, so you can keep challenging trainers for as long as it stays in the slot.

The trainer's level is matched to your party. The settings still live under battleseeker, the name of the item the Combat Basket replaced:

Setting Meaning /picnic config battleseeker matchlevel <true\|false> Scale the trainer to your party's level. Default on. /picnic config battleseeker levelgap <int> Level offset on top of the match, to make them tougher or softer. Default 8. /picnic config battleseeker enabled <true\|false> Off: a table with a Combat Basket summons nobody. Default on. /picnic config battleseeker blockinbattle <true\|false> On: the re-roll is refused while you are already in a battle. Default on.

No second fight on top of the first. While you are in a Cobblemon battle or a Cobblemon Action Combat fight (0.1.48 or later, optional), a Combat Basket table refuses the whole re-roll with "No trainer will come while you are already in a battle." and spends nothing. Switch it off with battleseeker blockinbattle false.

⚠️ The summon needs Radical Cobblemon Trainers (RCT) installed. Without it the Combat Basket simply does nothing and the rest of the table works normally.

The Battle Seeker is gone. It no longer turns up in chests and no longer does anything. One left in a table from before 5.0.0 shows in its old slot until you take it out.

docs.title: Colours, woods and fire
docs.text:
A picnic table is built in 16 cloth colours × 11 frame woods, with a wood per seat on top of that, and every piece it is made of is in the Creative inventory. All of them are flammable — they burn like wood planks, which is what the Nether exploits.

The tables and dining benches are furniture in their own right: you can sit on a bench, and a row of either joins up into one long piece as you place them.

docs.title: With Handcrafted or CobbleFurnies installed
docs.text:
Their furniture works in the picnic table recipe — every CobbleFurnies table, and Handcrafted's tables and benches — and the picnic table is drawn in whichever wood and cloth the piece you used is made of.

When one of those mods is there, the pieces of ours it already provides step aside: our dining benches go when Handcrafted is installed, and our oak tables go when CobbleFurnies is. They leave the creative tab and stop being craftable, so there is only ever one of each to pick from. The 160 wood-and-colour combinations stay — nothing else provides those — and anything you already built keeps working, because nothing is ever removed from the game.

Friendship built at the picnic stacks with normal Cobblemon mechanics, so it's a good way to evolve friendship-based Pokémon while you hunt.

docs.title: Picnic Tables
docs.text: Picnic Tables are the core block of the mod. Each is a 3×2 multiblock: the center column holds the table cells (re-roll + GUI), and the side cells are benches you can sit on, up to the tier's seat cap. Leftover side cells stay empty.

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text:
Tier Spawn cap Radius Seats Fuel / re-roll Basket slot Basic 5 32 2 7 bread Locked: keeps the basket it was crafted with Advanced 8 48 3 5 bread Locked: keeps the basket it was crafted with Expert 12 64 4 3 bread Swappable: takes every special basket
  • Spawn cap — the maximum Pokémon a single re-roll can spawn (and the GUI slider's max).
  • Radius — how far around the table wild Pokémon are despawned and re-rolled.
  • Seats — how many benches the footprint provides (seat counts are fixed per tier, not configurable).
  • Fuel — bread consumed per re-roll, cheaper as tiers improve (7 for Basic, 5 for Advanced, 3 for Expert). Bread comes from the table's fuel slot or from a nearby Picnic Basket. The per-tier cost is configurable (/picnic config reroll fuelcost <tier>).

Basic → Advanced → Expert is the whole ladder. What used to be the Diving, Hot and Strange tables are now baskets you put in an Expert table: see Baskets.

docs.title: Crafting
docs.text: A Picnic Table is built in two steps: craft the three components, then assemble them into the Basic Picnic Table. Higher tiers are upgrades of that one.

docs.title: 1. The components
docs.text:
Each one comes in every color or wood the table can be built from — the grids below show one example.

TableDining BenchPicnic Basket

The tabletop. Any of the 16 dye colors of wool over any of the 11 woods of planks — the wool is the cloth and the planks are the frame, so there are 176 of them (Red Table, Spruce Red Table, Cherry Black Table, …). Oak's are the ones with no wood in the name.

➜

Ingredient Amount Wool — any of the 16 colors 3 Planks — any of the 11 woods 2 → Table in that color and wood 1

The seat. Slabs and planks of the same wood — available in 11 woods: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, bamboo, crimson and warped.

➜ 2

Ingredient Amount Slab — any of the 11 woods 3 Planks of the same wood 2 → Dining Bench in that wood 2

Apricorns over apricorn planks, in a 2×2 corner of the grid. One per apricorn color — white, black, blue, green, pink, red and yellow.

➜

Ingredient Amount Apricorn — any of the 7 colors 2 Apricorn Planks 2 → Picnic Basket in that color 1

A basket is also useful on its own, as a bread store next to the table.

docs.title: 2. The Basic Picnic Table
docs.text:
➜ Ingredient Amount Accepts Picnic Basket 1 any of the 7 colors Vivichoke 1 — Table 2 any of the 176 — the left one sets the cloth colour and the frame wood. Tables from CobbleFurnies and Handcrafted work too Campfire Pot 1 any Cobblemon Campfire Pot, or Cobblemon's own Campfire Dining Bench 2 any of the 11 woods — each one becomes a seat, in the order you place them. Benches from Handcrafted work too Campfire 1 Campfire or Soul Campfire → Basic Picnic Table 1

The result is drawn as exactly the items you built it from: the cloth and the wood of the table you used, and a separate bench per seat — two benches of different woods come out as two different seats. All of it with the mod's own models and textures, so no other furniture mod is required. The basket you crafted it with starts in the table's basket slot and stands beside the table in its colour; the pot and campfire are consumed but don't change how the table looks.

Hold Shift over a picnic table in your inventory to read back everything it is made of.

docs.title: 3. Upgrading
docs.text:
The three higher tiers are shapeless — the ingredients can sit anywhere in the grid. An upgrade keeps the colour and the woods the table was crafted with, and it adds a seat: the bench you hand over is the bench that seat is made of. A table can end up with four seats in four woods.

AdvancedExpert

➜

Ingredient Amount Basic Picnic Table 1 Diamond 1 Dining Bench — any wood 1 → Advanced Picnic Table 1

➜

Ingredient Amount Advanced Picnic Table 1 Netherite Ingot 1 Dining Bench — any wood 1 → Expert Picnic Table 1

docs.title: Dyeing
docs.text:
A table that is already placed can be recoloured without picking it up. Hold a dye and sneak + right-click:

  • The top of a table repaints its cloth, in any of the 16 dye colours. A picnic table is two tables side by side, and only the one you clicked changes — the two can wear different colours.
  • The table's basket repaints the basket, in any of the 7 basket colours: white, black, blue, green, pink, red and yellow. A special basket keeps its emblem. Any other dye does nothing to it.

The wood never takes a dye. The benches and the frame keep the woods the table was crafted with, and clicking them with a dye does nothing.

Each repaint uses up one dye, and none is spent on something that is already that colour. Sneaking is what makes it a dye: without it, the click does what it always does.

A loose Picnic Basket can be dyed the same way.

docs.title: Baskets
docs.text:
Every table has a basket slot next to the bread in its screen, and a new table starts with the basket it was crafted with. What sits in that slot decides what the table does.

  • On an Expert table the basket swaps. Click a basket onto the slot and the old one comes back to you. A basket never comes out on its own, only swapped for another one.
  • On Basic and Advanced tables the basket is locked — a padlock on the slot. It stays the plain basket the table was crafted with, so the special baskets are an Expert table's business.

docs.title: The special baskets
docs.text:
Each one is any Picnic Basket plus one ingredient, shapeless. It keeps the basket's apricorn colour and gets an emblem on the front; the basket drawn on the table is the one in the slot, colour and emblem, and it gives off a few particles of its kind.

Basket Recipe In an Expert table Water Basket 💧 basket + heart of the sea The table is at home underwater Fire Basket 🔥 basket + fire charge The table is at home in the Nether Strange Basket 👁️ basket + eye of ender The table is at home in the End Alpha Basket basket + ghast tear Every Pokémon a re-roll spawns has a 10% chance to be an alpha, but only half the batch spawns (rounded up) Combat Basket ⚔️ basket + iron sword Every re-roll also summons an RCT trainer to battle — see Combat Basket

Alpha Basket. The table screen shows the smaller batch in gold, and alphas turn up in the re-roll log and in /picnic stats. Each one is a full alpha, the same as one from a Hopo Berry seasoning: it gets its alpha moveset, matches its level to nearby players like a natural alpha and shows as alpha right away. The Alpha Basket only fits an Expert table. An operator changes the chance and the batch with /picnic config alphaboost.

Alpha and Combat baskets are for Overworld picnics. They carry no home of their own, so their table is a plain Expert table: it burns in the Nether and drifts in the End. A table holds one basket, so alpha hunting and RCT trainers only work in the Overworld. The baskets' tooltip says so too.

Placed on its own, a special basket keeps its emblem and drops back as the same basket. It still stores bread like any Picnic Basket.

docs.title: Where each table can go
docs.text:
Any table can be placed in any dimension. Where a table goes is your business — what the place does to it once it is standing there is the dimension's.

A Water, Fire or Strange basket makes an Expert table belong somewhere, and carry that somewhere with it. At home it is simply a table. Anywhere else it inflicts on its surroundings exactly what an ordinary table suffers where that home is native: fire scorches, strange will not sit still, water floods.

Table Overworld Nether The End Any table without a dimension basket ✅ ⚠️ catches fire ⚠️ drifts away Expert + Water Basket 🌊 floods on each re-roll (on dry land) 🔥 burns at once 🌊 floods · ⚠️ drifts away Expert + Fire Basket 🔥 scorches on each re-roll ✅ at home 🔥 scorches · ⚠️ drifts away Expert + Strange Basket ⚠️ drifts away ⚠️ drifts · catches fire ✅ at home

🔥 An ordinary table burns in the Nether. Leave any table without a Fire basket down there and it has a 30% chance every second of a flame taking hold on it. Nothing is destroyed outright — it burns from there under the normal fire rules, so you can still put it out. A Water basket is the exception in the other direction: a tableful of water in that heat goes up the moment it arrives. To picnic in the Nether properly, bring a Fire basket: nothing sets that table alight, anywhere.

🌡️ The Fire basket takes the Nether with it. Anywhere else, each re-roll scorches the ground around the table: its heat reaches 6 blocks out, lights many blocks at once and sets every creature in reach on fire for 8 seconds — including whoever is sitting at it. It is a basket for the Nether, and taking it home is supposed to be a bad idea.

🌊 The Water basket takes the water with it. Out of the water, each re-roll flushes the ring of blocks around the table with flowing water (never the table itself). Nothing feeds it, so it drains on its own and leaves the floor clean. Underwater it just sits there, because there is nothing left to spill. Expert tables can be placed in water, so you can set one on the sea floor and put the Water basket in afterwards; Basic and Advanced tables still refuse water.

🌌 The End will not hold a picnic still, and the Strange basket will not sit still anywhere else. Sit down at any table without a Strange basket out there, or try to re-roll at it, and the whole table is somewhere else within 24 blocks before the click lands — leaving you standing where it used to be. Nothing is lost: the bread and the basket, the cloth colour and the woods it was crafted with, and your Pokémon-per-re-roll setting all travel with it. A table with nowhere to go — walled in, or ringed by void — stays put and works normally. To picnic in the End properly, bring a Strange basket: that table never drifts.

A server that wants none of this switches it all off with /picnic config hazards enabled false. Every table is then plain furniture, wherever it stands.

docs.title: Diving, Hot and Strange tables from before 5.0.0
docs.text:
Those three tables can no longer be crafted and are gone from the creative tab. One already placed in a world turns into an Expert table with the matching Water, Fire or Strange basket in its slot the first time it loads, keeping its bread and its look. If it already held a basket of another kind, that basket stays and the dimension basket drops beside the table.

Water, Fire and Strange baskets from before 5.0.0 (one colour each) turn into the coloured basket with that emblem by themselves.

docs.title: Placement & orientation
docs.text:
The table deploys in front of you, with the table column centred on where you aim, oriented to your facing — the "wide" axis runs left-to-right relative to you. The structure is one block tall: benches on the sides, the functional table down the middle. All six cells must be free, and each table needs its own footprint, since overlapping structures interfere with each other's cells.

To pick it back up, break a bench. Table cells take no mining damage — that's what keeps a re-roll from destroying the table you're clicking. Breaking any bench takes the whole structure and returns the table item.

The basket stays inside it. The table item that drops carries its basket, kind included, and everything the table was built from, so placing it again brings both back. The bread in the slot spills, and so does a leftover Battle Seeker. Tables from the creative tab come with a red basket.

docs.title: Shiny Aura
docs.text:
Picnics are better with friends — and more friends means more shinies.

Sit on a table's benches and everyone seated gets their shiny odds multiplied. A full table doubles them. Every seat is worth exactly the same share of that bonus, so the ladder is easy to read:

Seated Your shiny odds At Cobblemon's default 1/8192 1 ×1.25 ≈ 1 in 6554 2 ×1.50 ≈ 1 in 5461 3 ×1.75 ≈ 1 in 4681 4 ×2.00 ≈ 1 in 4096

Each person is worth +0.25×, and a full table is ×2.00 — that's the one number you can change (see Tuning below); the rungs in between are always split evenly.

A full table means four seats, which is what an Expert table provides. A smaller table simply stops earlier: Basic seats 2 and tops out at ×1.50, Advanced seats 3 and tops out at ×1.75. Sometimes you need a bigger table, not more friends.

docs.title: It multiplies, it never replaces
docs.text: The aura is applied last, on top of whatever your odds already are — your server's shiny rate, a Shiny Charm, anything else. ×2.00 means "twice as likely as you were a moment ago", whatever that was. It can only ever improve your odds.

docs.title: Where you can see it
docs.text:
• A ring of particles hovers above the table, denser the fuller the table is.

  • The HUD (top right) reads your live aura in two lines:

    Shiny Aura ✦ ×1.50 odds
    2/4 seated · 1 in 5461

    It hides with F1, like the rest of the HUD.

  • Chat tells you the moment it changes — when you sit down, and again each time someone joins or leaves your table.

  • A "Shiny Aura" buff appears in your inventory; its level (I–IV) is how many of you are seated.

All of those numbers are calculated on the server, so on multiplayer you're reading its real settings, not a guess from your own config file.

docs.title: When the boost applies
docs.text: The aura stays live the whole time you're seated (it clears about a second after you stand up), and while it's live it improves any shiny roll Cobblemon attributes to you — the table's re-roll and the natural wild spawns that appear around you as you sit. Triggering a re-roll also grants the table's multiplier to whoever pressed it, for that roll.

docs.title: How to sit
docs.text: Right-click a bench cell (a side seat) with an empty hand to sit. Sneak or move to stand up. Seats are invisible mounts — you'll snap neatly onto the bench.

docs.title: Tuning
docs.text:
See Commands & Config:

Setting Meaning /picnic config shinyaura enabled <true\|false> Master on/off switch for the whole feature. /picnic config shinyaura multiplier <1..100> Shiny odds at a full table. Default 2 (double). 1 turns the aura off.

In Mod Menu it's the "Shiny odds at a full table (×)" field, which prints the resulting ladder right underneath as you type.

docs.title: Spawn Re-rolling
docs.text:
The headline feature. Left-click the center (table) cells and the table will:

  1. Despawn nearby wild Pokémon within the tier's radius — but never owned/tethered Pokémon (yours and other players' stay safe). A wild Pokémon that someone is battling, or that a Poké Ball is already flying at, is left alone too.
  2. Force a fresh "maximized" natural respawn around the table, using Cobblemon's own spawner at a boosted density so you get a full batch immediately.

This lets you re-roll the local spawns on demand — ideal for shiny hunting or fishing for a specific species without wandering the world.

docs.title: How many spawn?
docs.text:
Open the table's GUI and use the slider to choose how many Pokémon a re-roll spawns, up to the tier's spawn cap (Basic 5, Advanced 8, Expert 12). The re-roll counts the Pokémon that really landed and keeps drawing spots until it reaches that number or runs out of tries, and the "Spawned N fresh" message counts the same Pokémon the re-roll log lists. It never goes over the number: a group spawn that lands more than are still missing has the extras removed.

The basket in the table can change the batch: an Alpha Basket spawns only half (rounded up), each with a 10% chance to be an alpha, and the screen shows the smaller number in gold. A Combat Basket adds an RCT trainer.

docs.title: Where they appear
docs.text:
Spawns land inside the table's own radius, 6 blocks out to the tier's limit, and the search follows the ground at whatever spot it picks. That is what makes a re-roll work on a mountain top, a ledge or a slope, where the terrain a few blocks away sits well below your feet.

It also prefers ground near your own altitude. Stand on a summit and the re-roll fills the summit, not the valley below it — it only settles for lower ground when there's nothing else within reach, so a bare peak still gets its Pokémon.

Nothing spawns on the table, and nothing spawns within 2 blocks of you (change it with /picnic config reroll clearance), so a whole group never lands on the food or on your head.

Underground and underwater the search keeps your own altitude instead, so caves and tables with a Water basket behave the way you'd expect.

A single unlucky spot doesn't end the attempt — the table keeps picking new ones until it fills your order or runs out of tries. If a place genuinely has nowhere to put a Pokémon, it says so plainly rather than reporting a silent zero. The bread is still spent: the area was cleared either way, and that can't be undone.

docs.title: Next to a habitat
docs.text: Cobblemon 1.8 habitat blocks add their own pool to spawns within about 16 blocks of them. When a habitat's reach overlaps the table's radius, the re-roll looks for spawns inside it, so the habitat's pool (in its current phase) is what comes back: handy for hunting a Pokémon that is rare everywhere else. Habitats that run their own spawner (the "activated" kind) are left out, since they block every other spawner around them.

docs.title: Built platforms
docs.text:
Cobblemon only spawns most wild Pokémon on natural ground: grass, dirt, stone, sand. A table on a deck of planks, a quartz tower or a concrete floor has nowhere to put them, and the table says so, naming the ground that does work.

Turn on /picnic config platforms enabled true and a re-roll spawns on any floor. Which Pokémon come is unchanged: the biome under you, the time of day, the light and the height still decide. Only the "natural ground" rule is lifted, and only for the table's own re-roll; Cobblemon's normal spawning keeps its rules. On natural ground the switch changes nothing. It is off by default.

docs.title: Pokémon that fly, spawn flying
docs.text:
A re-rolled Pokémon whose species can fly is lifted 3 to 12 blocks off the ground it appeared on, as far as clear air allows. Set the ceiling with /picnic config reroll flyinglift (0 keeps everything on the ground).

And a flier that spawned on ground below you climbs to your own altitude. On a peak that's the difference between watching them circle your table and never seeing them at all, because the only ground for a hundred blocks was somewhere down the mountainside. Clear air still has the final say, so none of them end up inside the mountain.

They stay around the table. For 30 seconds after a re-roll, a flier that leaves the table's re-roll radius turns back toward the table, at your height. Inside the radius it flies wherever it likes, and once the time is up it is fully wild again. Over open sea this is what keeps a re-roll from flying out of sight before you get a look at it. Set the time with /picnic config reroll flierleash (0 lets them roam at once).

It doesn't change your odds. Lifting happens after the spawn is decided. Which Pokémon appear, and how often, is Cobblemon's call alone — its spawn pool, the biome, the light, and any poke_snack influence in range. Nothing is added, removed or re-rolled, so a shiny hunt runs at exactly the rate it always did.

docs.title: Fuel
docs.text:
Each re-roll costs bread, depending on tier:

Tier Bread per re-roll Basic 7 Advanced 5 Expert 3

Fuel gets cheaper as tiers improve. Bread can come from the table's fuel slot or from a nearby placed Picnic Basket — the table will pull from baskets automatically. Out of bread? The table tells you and the re-roll is cancelled. Each per-tier cost is configurable via /picnic config reroll fuelcost <tier> (see Commands & Config).

docs.title: Cooldown
docs.text: To stop a table being spammed, each re-roll starts a cooldown (default 5 seconds). It's enforced both per-table and per-player — whichever is still counting down blocks the re-roll, so you can't dodge it by hopping between tables. A blocked attempt shows a short actionbar countdown and costs no bread. Change it with /picnic config reroll cooldown <seconds> (0 disables the wait).

docs.title: Party move teaching
docs.text:
Every re-roll has a small chance (5% by default) that one of your party Pokémon teaches another party member one of its moves — a little picnic bonding. The teacher can pass on any move it has learned, in its battle four or benched. The student only takes a TM, tutor or egg move that is in its own learnset and that it hasn't learned yet, so it never gains an illegal move; if all four slots are full, one move is swapped out.

Tune it with /picnic config tmteach chance <0..1>, pick which kinds can be taught with /picnic config tmteach tm|tutor|egg <true|false> (all three on by default), or switch it off with /picnic config tmteach enabled false.

docs.title: Snack bias
docs.text: If a seasoned poke_snack is nearby when you re-roll, the spawn respects that snack's spawn influence (so you can bias toward what the snack attracts) and consumes one bite of the closest snack. See Interactions & Items → Snacks.

docs.title: Do the table's boosts stack with shiny and alpha seasonings?
docs.text:
Yes, but they add up rather than multiply. Cobblemon rolls a seasoning as its own extra chance, separate from the normal shiny or alpha roll, so the table's boost and the seasoning are two independent chances on the same Pokémon.

  • Shiny: the Shiny Aura improves the normal shiny roll. A shiny seasoning (Starf Berry, Golden Apple, Enchanted Golden Apple) then gives a second roll that always uses the server's base shiny rate, so the aura does not make the seasoning itself stronger. The Shiny Charm does not boost the seasoning either.
  • Alpha: the Hopo Berry seasoning gives each spawn a 2% alpha chance. The Alpha Basket then rolls its own chance (10% by default) on every spawn that is not already an alpha.

At the default shiny rate of 1/8192, with the aura at ×2:

Setup Shiny odds per Pokémon Aura ×2 only about 1/4096 Starf Berry only about 1/1640 Aura ×2 + Starf Berry about 1/1170 Aura ×2 + Golden Apple about 1/2050 Aura ×2 + Enchanted Golden Apple about 1/680

For alphas, the Alpha Basket plus a Hopo Berry snack gives about 11.8% per Pokémon, against 10% for the basket alone.

Owned Pokémon are always safe. The despawn step skips anything with an owner, so you can leave your party out — or a pasture nearby — and re-roll freely.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common surprises, what causes them, and what to do. If yours isn't here, post it in the Discord — it files the ticket for you.

docs.title: The game won't start and names Cobblemon
docs.text: Picnic needs Cobblemon 1.8.0 or newer. Install or update Cobblemon; nothing else needs changing.

docs.title: A re-roll cleared the area but spawned nothing
docs.text:
The table tells you which of two things went wrong:

  • "…nothing spawns on built ground." You're on a built floor: planks, bricks, quartz, concrete, glass, wool. Cobblemon only spawns on natural ground (grass, dirt, stone, sand). Put down some natural blocks, or turn on built platforms with /picnic config platforms enabled true.
  • "…there was nowhere around here to spawn any." There's no ground near your altitude inside the table's radius, for example a tiny platform over the void. Make the platform bigger, or widen the table's reach with /picnic config reroll radius <tier> <blocks>.

Over an ocean or a river the message names the biome, because the biome decides which Pokémon can come at all. The bread is spent either way: the area was cleared, and that can't be undone.

docs.title: The table said it spawned Pokémon, but I can't see them
docs.text: Fliers take off. For 30 seconds after a re-roll a flier that leaves the table's radius turns back, so look up and around. If you set flierleash to 0, they roam at once. See Pokémon that fly.

docs.title: "The table is still resting…"
docs.text: There's a cooldown (5 seconds by default) per table and per player. Swapping tables doesn't skip it. The blocked attempt costs no bread. An operator can change it with /picnic config reroll cooldown <seconds>.

docs.title: "Out of bread!"
docs.text: Each re-roll costs bread (7 / 5 / 3 by tier). It comes from the table's fuel slot or from a placed Picnic Basket nearby.

docs.title: My settings screen changes do nothing on a server
docs.text: The Mod Menu / Cloth Config screen edits your own config file. On someone else's server the server's settings win, and the screen says so. Ask an operator to use /picnic config.

docs.title: A table with a Water, Fire or Strange basket wrecks things
docs.text: Those baskets are built for one place: underwater, the Nether, the End. Anywhere else each re-roll floods or scorches around the table, and the Strange one won't stay put. See where each table can go. Swap the basket on an Expert table, or an operator can turn it all off with /picnic config hazards enabled false.

docs.title: My Diving, Hot or Strange table became an Expert table
docs.text: That's 5.0.0: those tables are now baskets. An old one turns into an Expert table with the matching basket in its slot the first time it loads, and works exactly as before.

docs.title: I can't put a special basket in my table
docs.text: Basic and Advanced tables keep the basket they were crafted with (the slot shows a padlock). Water, Fire, Strange, Alpha and Combat baskets go in an Expert table.

docs.title: Reporting a bug
docs.text: Every re-roll is written to logs/latest.log (unless /picnic config reroll log false): what was cleared and what spawned, with species, level and position. Attach that part of the log to a report and it already says what happened.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Re-rolls never guarantee a shiny. The table only asks Cobblemon to spawn again; the odds are Cobblemon's, improved only by the Shiny Aura.
  • Seat counts are fixed per tier and can't be configured.
